# Neuro-Symbolic Integration and Emergent Compositionality {#sec-ch-neurosymbolic-integration}

This chapter is a stub. Its outline follows the roadmap in [index.qmd](../index.qmd) and exists so that other chapters can already cross-reference its sections.

## The Systematicity Challenge
*Fodor and Pylyshyn's argument that thought is compositional, the connectionist replies, and the staircase of @sec-ch-symbols-without-interior revisited: which steps can a vector system climb? Cross-modal models give a concrete test: image-text models that retrieve a "dog" and a "man" but confuse "dog bites man" with "man bites dog".*

## The Poverty of the Stimulus
*Chomsky's argument (1965, 1980) that children receive too little data to learn grammar unless much of it is innate, the bitter-lesson debate in the vocabulary of linguistics, with recursion as the core of the language faculty (Hauser, Chomsky, and Fitch, 2002). Told as a historical sequence on the standard example, structure-dependent question formation ("Is the man who is tall happy?"): sequential networks generalize linearly and only tree-structured ones hierarchically (2020); vanilla transformers learn the hierarchical rule long after in-domain accuracy saturates, "structural grokking" (2023); GPT-2 learns humanly impossible languages less easily than possible ones, against Chomsky's claim (2024); and the BabyLM challenge (2023) sets the budget at the fewer than 100 million words a child hears by age 13.*
